method: Same as E12b (nearest resize) at 216 px instead of 144 px
explanation: Val accuracy 0.975 - same as E8 (0.976, bicubic 224). At high resolution the filter no longer matters: large files 0.990 in both, 72 px files 0.964 vs 0.966. The nearest advantage of E12b was a low-resolution effect (bicubic downscaling to 144 blurs detail; at ~216-224 enough detail survives either way). Value is as an ensemble member: E8+E12b+E13 = 0.981 val, best combination - but 11 combinations were compared on the same validation set and they span 0.977-0.981 (differences of 1-8 images), so the pick carries selection bias.
preprocessing: Alpha-composite on white background, then resize to 216x216 with NEAREST neighbour, ImageNet normalisation
preprocessing_why: E12b showed nearest > bicubic (+0.9 pts) and E8 showed higher resolution helps (+1.7 pts). 216 = exact 3x of the 72 px files, close to the 224 px of E8 and to the native 240 px of the large files.
